Successful Qt destruction recording covers shown nonmodal real DialogEdit/FleshOutPredicatePanel under standalone QWidget.window() owners with retained Python wrappers, unchanged blank predicates and DeferredDelete draining. It does not destroy client Main, exercise active DialogEdit exec() or establish active nested static-warning teardown. Native cleanup-notice closure is a separate safety boundary.

Native retirement automatically hides the owned editor/notice and permanently refuses callbacks while retained Slint components/adapters remain alive; this is not Qt invalid-wrapper/object-deallocation parity. Main alone is hidden to release shown-platform retention before actual drop; no child/notice manual closure precedes automatic proof.

Main destruction is observed by repeated50ms owner polling and requires event-loop pumping (tests bounded<=2s); final Bound-owner drop retires synchronously. Nonfinal Bound clones, temporary Main hide and pending/declined exit preserve drafts. Retained warning adapters/windows are tested; the private SessionDialog component is not separately exposed.

Native dedicated editor/notice captures preserve the finite controls/messages but differ from Qt in font metrics, spacing, input height/width, star/icon styling, large vertical notice OK and outer Apply footer topology. No whole-dialog pixel/geometry equality, OS chrome/modality/focus, clipboard bitmap equality or arbitrary shared-editor ownership is claimed.
Validation is Linux only; Windows and macOS are deferred. No parent, alias, generic active-edit, global-radio or additional-family completion credit.
